title: General Import Documentation
canonical_question: What documents do I need for import?
query_variations: What documents do I need to import goods?
What paperwork is required for importing?
Which documents are needed for an import shipment?
What import documentation do I need?
What docs do I need to bring goods into the country?
What papers are required to clear imported cargo?
What documentation is needed for customs clearance?
Which paperwork should I prepare for an incoming shipment?
Do I need papers to import?
answer: Commonly required import documents include a Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, and an Arrival Notice. Depending on the shipment's origin and cargo type, additional documents such as a Certificate of Origin or specific import permits may be required.

title: General Export Documentation
canonical_question: What documents do I need for export?
query_variations: What paperwork is needed to export goods?
Which documents are required for an export shipment?
What export documentation do I need?
What docs do I need to send goods out of the country?
What papers are required to ship goods overseas?
Which paperwork should I prepare for an outgoing shipment?
What do I need to export cargo?
answer: Export shipments typically require a Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and a transport document (Bill of Lading or Air Waybill). Depending on the destination and the goods, you may also need an Export Declaration, Certificate of Origin, or specific export permits.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Customs Duty Calculation
query_variations: How much customs will I pay?
What tax is charged on imports?
How expensive will clearing my goods be?
Will I pay duty on this shipment?
How do customs calculate what I owe?
What import charges should I expect?
How much tax will I be charged on imported goods?
answer: Customs duties are generally calculated based on the Harmonized System (HS) code of the goods, their declared value, the country of origin, and the destination country's tariff schedule. Rates vary significantly depending on these factors.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

canonical_question: Why is my shipment stuck in customs?

Why is clearance taking too long?
Why is my package held up?
answer: Shipments may be held by customs due to missing or incorrect documentation, random physical inspections, unpaid duties, or regulatory compliance checks. Your customs broker can advise you on the specific reason.

title: Harmonized System Classification
query_variations: What product code do I need?
How do I classify my goods?
Where can I find my HS number?
What's the customs classification for my product?
answer: An HS (Harmonized System) code is an internationally standardized system of names and numbers to classify traded products. It determines the applicable duty rates, taxes, and regulatory requirements for your cargo.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Commercial Invoice Requirements
canonical_question: What information must be on a Commercial Invoice?
query_variations: What needs to be included in a commercial invoice?
How to fill out a commercial invoice?
What details go on the invoice for customs?
Do I need HS codes on the invoice?
answer: A Commercial Invoice must include the buyer and seller details, a detailed description of the goods, HS codes, unit prices, total value, currency, terms of sale (Incoterms), and country of origin.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Incoterms Overview
query_variations: What's the difference between FOB and CIF?
Who pays for freight and insurance?
What do three letter shipping codes mean?
answer: Incoterms (International Commercial Terms) are standardized rules published by the ICC that define the responsibilities of buyers and sellers under sales contracts. They dictate exactly who is responsible for paying freight, insurance, and customs clearance.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance.

title: FCL vs LCL
canonical_question: What is the difference between FCL and LCL?
query_variations: Should I use FCL or LCL?
Difference between full container and less than container?
How do I ship a small amount of cargo?
Is it cheaper to ship FCL or LCL?
answer: FCL (Full Container Load) means you rent an entire container for your goods, which is faster and safer. LCL (Less than Container Load) means your goods share a container with other shippers, which is more cost-effective for smaller volumes but takes longer due to consolidation.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance.

title: Packing Lists
query_variations: What goes on a packing list?
Do I need a packing slip?
answer: A packing list details the contents, dimensions, and weight of each package in a shipment. Customs uses it for physical inspections.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Bills of Lading
canonical_question: What is a Bill of Lading?
query_variations: Do I need an ocean bill of lading?
answer: A Bill of Lading (B/L) is a legal document issued by an ocean carrier acknowledging receipt of cargo. It acts as a receipt, contract, and document of title.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Air Waybills
query_variations: Is an air waybill the same as a bill of lading?
answer: An Air Waybill (AWB) is a non-negotiable transport document issued by an airline. Unlike a B/L, it is not a document of title.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Certificates of Origin
canonical_question: Do I need a Certificate of Origin?
query_variations: Do I need a form to claim free trade benefits?
answer: A Certificate of Origin (COO) may be required by destination customs to verify where the goods were manufactured, often to claim reduced tariffs under Free Trade Agreements.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Import Permits
canonical_question: Do I need an import permit?
query_variations: Do I need a license to import?
answer: Certain restricted goods (like agriculture, pharmaceuticals, or hazardous materials) require special government import permits before entering the country.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Export Permits
canonical_question: Do I need an export permit?
query_variations: Do I need a license to export?
answer: Export permits may be required for controlled goods, dual-use technology, or military equipment. Requirements depend strictly on the origin country.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Demurrage
query_variations: Why am I being charged demurrage?
answer: Demurrage is a fee charged by the terminal for leaving a full container at the port beyond the allotted free time.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance.

title: Detention
query_variations: Why am I being charged detention?
What happens if I return the container late?
answer: Detention is a fee charged by the carrier for keeping their empty equipment (the container) outside the port beyond the allotted free time.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance.

title: Chargeable Weight
query_variations: Why is my chargeable weight higher than actual?
answer: Chargeable weight is calculated based on either the actual gross weight or the volumetric (dimensional) weight, whichever is greater.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance.

title: Freight Insurance
query_variations: What happens if my cargo sinks?
answer: Yes. Carriers only offer limited liability coverage. Comprehensive freight insurance protects you against total loss or damage during transit.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance.

title: Arrival Notice
query_variations: How do I know my cargo arrived?
answer: An Arrival Notice is a document issued by the carrier informing the consignee that the shipment has arrived or is about to arrive at the destination.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.

title: Letter of Credit
canonical_question: How does a Letter of Credit work?
query_variations: Shipping with a letter of credit?
answer: A Letter of Credit (L/C) is a bank guarantee of payment. All shipping documents must perfectly match the L/C terms, or payment may be delayed or refused.
disclaimer: This chatbot provides general informational guidance. Specific requirements should be verified with the relevant customs authority.
